candidates.above_next: It is the frame every other principle presupposes; code-as-data is powerful but serves this, not the reverse.

also.why: it takes a stance: belonging to a type must mean a guarantee, not a mere tag.

beats.why: compile-time rejection of invalid models is one consequence of the same idea, stated narrowly for one domain rather than as the organizing rule.

harms: punishes code whose guarantees cannot be stated as laws
can make every definition carry proof obligations it does not need
excludes quick prototyping where a bare value suffices
candidates.instead_of: types as mere storage shapes or tags with no semantic content
candidates.quote: los tipos tienen que ser conceptos, tipos como proposiciones y los tipos incluyen también funciones, funciones y funciones de orden superior
candidates.statement: A type is the proposition its values must satisfy, extended to functions whose type is their laws, so membership is a guarantee.

strongest.why: collapsing type, test and proposition into one thing reorganizes what it means to define anything, so a function's type is the law it obeys.

candidates.above_next: It is the mechanism that makes the construction pattern reusable across values, functions and whole programs alike.

also.why: he returns to it for fifteen years as the move that gives flexibility no modern language takes.

beats.why: first-class contexts are one technical realization of code-as-data, a narrower consequence than the general erasure of the distinction.

harms: homoiconicity invites self-hacking if eval injects arbitrary terms
a program manipulating its own code is harder to reason about
blurs a distinction many programmers rely on for safety
candidates.instead_of: a fixed boundary where source is compiled once and never seen as a value
candidates.quote: La idea de que el codigo sea dato es muy, pero muy fuerte en cuanto a la flexibilidad que ofrece pero es notable que los lenguajes modernos no sigan ese camino Lispeano.
candidates.statement: Code is a datum of the language itself, so a program can be built, inspected and run by other programs, and Luthier operates on Luthier.

strongest.why: erasing the code/data line lets the language operate on itself, so the interpreter, the trace and the verifier all become ordinary data.

candidates.above_next: It is the operative core where C1 becomes a mechanism; characterizing by the best object (next) is how its predicates should be written.

also.why: economy: the same construction serves values, functions and programs, with the subtype and its constructor two uses of one predicate.

beats.why: pre/postconditions are the same idea seen through one feature; the construction pattern names the general act they are instances of.

harms: every construction forced through a predicate check has a cost per build
a value you just want cheaply must pay the pattern
overgeneralizing one shape risks hiding domain differences
candidates.instead_of: ad hoc validation scattered at call sites, separate from the type
candidates.quote: este tipo Almacen que en realidad confunde dos cosas el constructor de almacen y el almacen es el concepto fundamental de Luthier (no almacen sino el patron de construccion).
candidates.statement: From a type and a predicate over it, derive a certified subtype, a validating constructor and the projection back, the one pattern for values, functions and programs.

strongest.why: one pattern (material type plus predicate yields certified type, validating constructor and forgetful projection) is read as the single core act the whole language is built from.

candidates.above_next: It tells you what to write in the laws; execution-as-verification (next) tells you what running them means.

also.why: choosing the invariant of the concept's type reframes every definition as a search for the object that represents it.

beats.why: levels of equivalence name distinctions this principle uses, but do not carry the imperative to characterize rather than reimplement.

harms: finding the best mathematical object is slow and may never settle
a wrong characterization is worse than an honest reimplementation
demands math literacy the everyday coder may lack
candidates.instead_of: laws that just restate what the fast code does (consistency, not characterization)
candidates.quote: La idea en realidad es buscar el objeto matematico que mejor lo represente y decirlo.
candidates.statement: For each concept find the mathematical object that best represents it and put it as the type's invariant, characterizing an operation rather than reproducing its implementation.

strongest.why: it says a law must state the property that determines an operation up to equality, not re-run its implementation, which is a discipline about what counts as a real invariant.

candidates.above_next: It frames why minimalism matters: a describing language needs only a tiny core to run by hand.

also.why: the whole language reduces to stating equivalences and then checking them, one idea doing double duty.

beats.why: the two-layer split (equivalence, then cost) is the architecture this principle implies, stated as a feature rather than as the governing idea.

harms: treating execution as verification downplays the real cost of running
delegating execution risks a gap between what is checked and what runs
a declarative-first stance can stall before anything executes
candidates.instead_of: a language whose primary act is to compile and run code
candidates.quote: Hay una idea, que la matemática no ejecuta, porque lo único que hace es verificar equivalencias. Entonces, bueno, sí, la ejecución en Luthier sería esa verificación de equivalencias
candidates.statement: Luthier first describes the problem and its equivalences and only then executes; execution is the verification of those equivalences, as mathematics verifies rather than runs.

strongest.why: reading execution as mathematics does, verifying equivalences, inverts the usual picture: the program describes and the run certifies, with a declarative and an executive side.

candidates.above_next: It bounds the machinery so that expressing the invariances of the disciplines (next) stays within a readable core.

also.why: a stance on what a language should be: small, self-extensible, with the minimalism in the founding components and the maximalism built from them.

beats.why: bridge language is one motive for minimalism; the executable-by-hand standard is the sharper, more infectious formulation of the same drive.

harms: few primitives push complexity into libraries that grow unwieldy
executable-by-hand can conflict with the speed real work needs
self-extensibility is a bootstrap burden before anything else
candidates.instead_of: a large built-in language with syntactic sugar and many primitives
candidates.quote: Luthier tendría que ser ejecutable a mano es decir que uno pudiese con l y papel escribir las cosas
candidates.statement: Keep the native core to a handful of primitives, self-extensible and executable by hand, and build every complex concept on top of it.

strongest.why: the demand that a well-written Luthier be executable by hand with pencil and paper is an austere standard of economy that shapes every primitive.

candidates.above_next: It gives the purpose; the hole (next) is the concrete device that lets an unexpressed invariance sit contained until filled.

also.why: reframing a language as a mechanism to express the invariants of a field, not to compute, opens a different purpose for programming.

beats.why: language of ideas is the same aspiration one level more abstract; expressing invariances is the concrete, more infectious version of it.

harms: aiming to express every discipline's invariances risks growing to encompass the universe
invariance-hunting can detach from any usable program
what counts as an invariance is itself a hard judgment
candidates.instead_of: a language organized around computation rather than meaning
candidates.quote: la idea de luthier es expresar invarianzas de los de las disciplinas
candidates.statement: Luthier is an abstraction mechanism whose aim is to express the invariances of the disciplines clearly.

strongest.why: it names what moves the author to invent the language: a relator of invariances, against the statistical predictor, a species mates within itself, electrons are fermions.

candidates.above_next: The hole marks what is not yet known; paths (next) organize the many ways a known function can be done.

also.why: no symbol is even needed: f : A -> B left undefined is already the hole, economy at its sharpest.

beats.why: forward and undefined types are the behavior the hole generalizes; the hole states it as one first-class citizen rather than a pair of cases.

harms: holes everywhere can hide how much is actually undefined
deferring bodies invites programs that never become executable
a first-class gap complicates reasoning about totality
candidates.instead_of: treating a missing definition as a compile error
candidates.quote: porque necesitamos el simbolo para el hueco, ?. No basta con decri f: A-> B y no definirlo?
candidates.statement: A declaration without a body is a first-class hole, an opaque name that does not reduce, and nothing executes until it is defined.

strongest.why: a bodyless declaration plays axiom, program input, external function, pending definition and dead code at once, so one construct absorbs five roles usually kept apart.

candidates.above_next: Choosing by expected loss only makes sense if the certificates it chooses over are strong, which is what sampled verification (next) must deliver.

also.why: the self-optimizing language, declarative and executive at once, is the vision he keeps returning to with evident pull.

beats.why: the Bayesian cost estimate is the technique that serves path selection; the paths idea is the structural reframing it supports.

harms: many implementations per function multiplies maintenance and testing
choosing by measured cost needs a reliable performance database
equivalence of paths is the hardest thing to prove
candidates.instead_of: one fixed implementation bound to a function name
candidates.quote: una funci esta funci puede ser implementada de muchas maneras, son los distintos paths y cada forma tiene una precisión y una velocidad
candidates.statement: A function has many equivalent implementations (paths), each with its precision and cost, and Luthier chooses among them by expected loss and speed.

strongest.why: one function with many implementations (paths), each with its precision and speed, chosen by expected loss, turns a program into a declarative object that self-optimizes.

also.why: it refuses to call a sampled result a proof: the certificate carries its level, proof and sampled at the limits of probability.

beats.why: levels of verification name the untested/tested distinction; the construct that unifies exact and statistical checking under one operation with a graded certificate is the more infectious formulation.

harms: sampled verification certifies a risk, never a universal truth
a tuned generator can make a false law pass
certificate and record proliferate if not pruned
candidates.instead_of: a single pass/fail notion of correctness
candidates.quote: La comprobación de un valor es un cómputo; la de una función es un experimento. Luthier tiene que tratar a los dos como la misma operación de construir, sabiendo que uno es exacto y el otro estadístico.
candidates.statement: Verification is one operation, exact when it can compute and statistical when it samples, and every value carries the grade of guarantee it was checked to.

strongest.why: treating checking a value and checking a function as one construct operation, exact or statistical, and reading verification as a Bayesian observer updating a posterior, makes the grade of guarantee part of what membership means.
